title: Topological Criteria for Hypothesis Testing with Finite-Precision Measurements
summary: We establish topological necessary and sufficient conditions under which a pair of statistical hypotheses can be consistently distinguished when i.i.d. observations are recorded only to finite precision. To accommodate finite-precision data, we introduce finite-precision tests: tests whose decision regions are open in the sample-space topology. We first show that, both for classical and finite-precision tests, the existence of such tests with finite-sample error control, asymptotic error control, or uniform convergence of the errors are all equivalent.
